quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Get used to using both brakes every time you slow down or stop. If you need to stop quickly, use both brakes. This will be easier if you practice it every time you brake.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride side-by-side.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation works well normally, riders should switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when making a turn, you should:

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite to the direction of the turn.
Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn a motorcycle, you must lean it. To make the motorcycle lean, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should turn their heads to look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
Turning your head gets other drivers' attention.
Mirrors are not helpful.
You should try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show, just like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should NOT:

options.text: Have scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be completely sealed.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be completely sealed.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, hard to break, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, and let air flow through. A sealed face shield will trap moisture, causing fogging that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it has all of these qualities, EXCEPT:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Fits snugly.
Has no defects.
Looks attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no visible defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to passing in a car. However:

options.text: Being visible is more important on a motorcycle than in a car.
Being visible is less important on a motorcycle than in a car.
Pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible is more important on a motorcycle than in a car.
questions.explanation: While the basic passing rules are the same as for cars, visibility is more important on a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily disappear into another vehicle's blind spot or be overlooked by drivers.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: To stop other drivers from trying to share your lane, ride in the center portion of your lane.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, you should check all of the following, EXCEPT the:

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Under normal road and traffic conditions, riders should keep a minimum ______ following distance.

options.text: One-second
Two-second
Three-second
Four-second

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-second
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least a two-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance whenever conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should the motorcycle and rider do?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider should lean at the same angle together. For slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) level makes a person legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person is considered legally intoxicated at a BAC of 0.08 percent. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from the elements
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting the distance ridden in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: On long rides, take frequent breaks to rest and avoid riding more than six hours per day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not use artificial stimulants because the effects can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: When you approach a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then slowly move forward to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then slowly move forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, stop first. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the road while looking.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
Begin slowing later than usual.
Apply the brakes more firmly than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes more softly than usual to keep from overworking them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds extra weight and affects how your motorcycle handles. You will need extra space to stop completely.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire provides power, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making mirrors hard to use.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and use your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you are riding too fast when shifting into a lower gear, the motorcycle will lurch and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: How do brightly-colored helmets help riders?

options.text: They make it easier for others to see the rider.
They can be distracting.
They do not improve a rider's visibility.
They are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make it easier for others to see the rider.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects your head in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of proper lane positioning?

options.text: It helps you see and be seen.
It helps you avoid road hazards.
It helps you avoid traffic signals.
It shows other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from hazards, wind blasts, and blind spots. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which gives a rider the best face protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that will not shatter protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What is the safest way to cross railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
You cannot cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Cross the tracks by riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, ride straight across within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you might enter another lane of traffic.
